sections.h2: Who records deeds in Wyoming County, PA?
sections.html:
In Wyoming County a single elected officeholder serves as both Register of Wills and Recorder of Deeds, working from the courthouse in the county seat, Tunkhannock. Every deed and mortgage on a county parcel is filed there, alongside estate paperwork.

Counter service runs weekdays from 8:30 to 4:00, with the last filing taken at 3:45 in the afternoon. Call (570) 996-2361 with questions. Only cash and checks are taken. Electronic recording, electronic filing and e-signatures are all unavailable, so whoever closes your sale must hand-deliver or mail the paper deed bearing original signatures.

The recorder's land records start in 1842, when the county was created out of Luzerne County. Papers filed before February 2007 are cited by book and page, while later ones use an instrument number. Either reference will bring up the deed by which you took title, using the online deed search on the county website.

sections.h2: What are the recording fees at the Wyoming County courthouse?
sections.html:
Filing a deed costs $64.75 at base, according to the county's schedule dated December 1, 2025. That amount is good for four pages and four names. A fifth page and beyond adds $2.00 apiece, and extra names beyond four add $0.50 apiece.

Charges for the other papers that tend to accompany a sale appear below. The recorder's website also announced a $20 flat lien search fee and a $30 base fee for maps starting November 1, 2026, and said the full schedule would be revised then, so request the current sheet before writing your check.

Wyoming County Recorder of Deeds base fees, schedule effective December 1, 2025 (source: county fee schedule)
DocumentBase fee
Deed$64.75
Mortgage$64.75
Satisfaction of mortgage$61.75
Release or assignment of mortgage$59.75
Easement$59.75
Affidavit or power of attorney$18.50
Military discharge (DD-214)No charge

Pay the exact sum. Anything over by $5.00 or less stays with the county, a larger overpayment gets the document sent back, and there are no refunds. Checks go to the order of the Wyoming County Recorder of Deeds.

sections.h2: How much is realty transfer tax on a Wyoming County sale?
sections.html:
Expect 2 percent in total, according to the county recorder: one point goes to the state and one point to local government. Harrisburg's Department of Revenue confirms the 1 percent state piece and says recorders gather it along with local tax.

Take a $215,400 price, the same as the county's Census median home value. The tax would come to $4,308. No deed is accepted until the tax is in hand. Here a single check can cover a taxable transaction, with no separate check for the tax.

Gifts inside the family can be exempt: the recorder's FAQ names husband and wife, parent and child, grandparent and grandchild, and siblings. It also suggests talking to an attorney before counting on that. Whenever an exemption is claimed, or the price paid differs from the one printed on the deed, a Statement of Value form must go in with two copies.

sections.h2: What must a deed look like to be recorded in Wyoming County?
sections.html:
Pages that break the formatting or notary rules come back unrecorded, so have the deed checked before it leaves your hands. The published list includes:

  • Ink signatures with a notary acknowledgment that is not dated before the deed. Photocopies are refused.
  • Font size 9 or bigger, half an inch of clear space at the top of each page, black and white only, and no staples.
  • The property's municipality, county and state written out, and a price in words that agrees with the price in figures.
  • A signed certification of address attached to each deed and mortgage.
  • A stamped return envelope, addressed to you and big enough for the original.

No parcel or PIN number is needed on a Wyoming County deed. Two cases add paperwork. A parcel spanning several municipalities calls for a Statement of Value giving the whole-number share of local tax for each. A taxable sale in Windham Township calls for one too, so the school district is correct.

To fix an earlier deed, a corrective or confirmatory deed has to carry a Statement of Value, say why it is being corrected, and attach the old deed. The recorder also points out that it does not vouch for what a document says. Staff confirm only that the rules are met and the fees and taxes are paid.

sections.h2: How soon do I get the deed back, and where can I see records?
sections.html:
A recorded original typically returns by mail about a week later, workload permitting, since staff proof, scan, index and verify each one. Names on a recorded deed cannot be added, dropped or altered by the office. Only a newly drafted deed can do that.

The courthouse computers and the county's online deed search both let you look through the records. Certified copies run $5.00 through eight pages and $0.50 for each page beyond. Staff look up documents by full name only. To trace an owner from a parcel number or street address, turn to the county GIS site or phone the assessment office.

Liens are split between offices. This one records mortgages and UCC filings. Other liens and judgments sit with the Prothonotary, the Clerk of Courts or Orphans' Court, so a seller worried about judgments needs to search those too.

sections.h2: What kind of place is Wyoming County for a house sale?
sections.html:
Rural Wyoming County covers roughly 397 square miles of land in the northeastern corner of the state. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 25,790 people, a drop of 1.1 percent since 2020. Five boroughs (Tunkhannock, Factoryville, Nicholson, Meshoppen and Laceyville) sit among the townships, and 95.3 percent of people live in areas the 2020 census classed as rural.

The Susquehanna's North Branch cuts through the county and the ground is hilly, with Mehoopany, Tunkhannock, Knob and Bowman's mountains filling some of it. US 6, US 11 and PA 29 are among the through roads. Tunkhannock averages about 25 degrees in January and 71 in July, so an inspector will look hard at roofs, plumbing and heating.

  • Housing units counted in 2025: 12,989.
  • Share of homes lived in by their owners: 77.9 percent, 2020 to 2024.
  • Middle-of-the-market value for those homes: $215,400.
  • Typical gross rent: $943 a month.
  • Household income at the midpoint: $72,460, with 24.3 percent of people aged 65 or over.

These numbers are from Census QuickFacts. When many owners are older, houses often pass through estates, and the Register of Wills half of this same office handles letters and the inheritance tax forms for them.

faqs.q: Does Wyoming County accept e-recording for deeds?
faqs.a: No. The Recorder of Deeds states that it does not accept e-recording, e-filing or e-signatures. Deliver the paper deed in person or by mail, with original notary signatures and a self-addressed stamped return envelope.

faqs.q: What is the realty transfer tax rate in Wyoming County?
faqs.a: It is 2 percent of the price, split 1 percent state and 1 percent local, according to the county's fee schedule and FAQ. The deed is not accepted until the tax is paid, and the office takes one check for one taxable transaction.

faqs.q: Do I need a parcel number to record my deed in Wyoming County?
faqs.a: No. The recorder says it does not require or certify PIN numbers. It does require the municipality, county and state on the document, and a Statement of Value when land lies in several municipalities or in Windham Township.

faqs.q: How much does the Wyoming County recorder charge for a mortgage satisfaction?
faqs.a: A satisfaction piece is $61.75 on the schedule effective December 1, 2025, which covers four pages and four names. A mortgage release or assignment is $59.75. Lenders usually file the satisfaction, and the recorder cannot do it for you.

faqs.q: Where do I find who owns a property in Wyoming County?
faqs.a: Use the county GIS website or call the assessment office, which can look up ownership by parcel number or address. The recorder can only search by full name, and the online deed search shows recorded documents back to 1842.
